title: Delegated team admins, centralized email filtering, and domain attestation
creator: Jordan Kim
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements a combined admin controls feature set: (1) delegated team admin roles that allow org admins to grant team-level management without broad org permissions, (2) a centralized email filtering engine (allowlist/denylist + heuristics) applied at invite time and via console bulk operations, and (3) a domain attestation workflow to automate and surface verified domains for invite routing and SSO constraints.

Goals:
- Integrate delegated team admin scopes with RBAC v2 so team admins can invite, remove, and manage membership within their scope but cannot alter org-level policies.
- Replace scattered invite checks with a single email-policy service that enforces allowlist/denylist, regex rules, and SAML attribute-based overrides at both API and Console flows.
- Provide a domain attestation flow: DNS TXT verification and optional automated once-off verification via SAML IdP assertion. Verified domains should be surfaced in Console and used by invite policies.
- Emit structured audit events for all admin actions and invite outcomes for SOC/forensics and billing reconciliation.

Design Notes / Decisions:
- RBAC v2 integration: We will add a new permission scope "team:members.manage" and a delegation model on Team objects. Team admins are granted a role that maps to a scoped permission which the runtime enforces via the existing RBAC middleware.
- Invite policy engine: Centralized microservice (email-policy-service) with a lightweight rules DSL: allowlist, denylist, domain-allow, domain-deny, regex rules, and auto-block scoring. Console and API will call the service synchronously during invite creation.
- Domain attestation: Two verification modes: DNS TXT (recommended) and SAML assertion (IdP-provided attestation). Each verified domain record stored as domain:status in the org config and exposed to policies.
- SSO/SAML interplay: When a tenant is SAML-enabled, attributes like "employeeType" and "groups" can override invite policy (e.g., auto-allow if SAML assertion includes "@company.com" claim and matches domain). Must be opt-in.
- Audit logging: Create new event types audit.event.admin_invite_attempt, audit.event.team_admin_action, audit.event.domain_verified with structured fields: actor, target_email, outcome, policy_id, rule_hit, ip, trace_id. Log to central audit store and include in per-org export.
- Migration: Existing org-level invite policies will be migrated into the new email-policy-service. Admins will be shown a migration review screen in Console with diff and fallback options.

API/Console changes (examples):
- API: POST /orgs/{org}/invites -> validation will now return 422 with policy violation details {"policy_id":"p-123","rule":"deny_regex","message":"personal email addresses not allowed"}.
- Console: Team settings page will have "Team Admins" section to add delegated admins and a "Manage Invite Policy" UI to preview policy behavior on a sample list.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Team admin role created and enforced: tests prove a team admin can manage members but cannot change org-wide settings.
- Email-policy-service evaluates invites with 95% accuracy on internal test corpus and rejects/flags as expected.
- Domain attestation flow implemented with success path for DNS TXT and SAML assertion; domain status displayed in Console.
- Audit events emitted for every invite attempt and team-admin action and visible in org audit exports.
- Migration path is available and tested in staging for 10 orgs, with opt-out.

Security & Compliance Notes:
- Verified domains are authoritative for policy routing and must be protected from tampering. Domain verification changes will require an entry into the audit log and an approver flow for orgs with compliance mode.
- Data retention for invite-related audit events follows org settings; ensure encryption-at-rest and access controls.

Implementation Plan (high level):
1) Backend: implement email-policy-service + RBAC scope changes + audit event schemas (2 sprints).
2) Console: Team admin UI + policy editor + migration screens (1 sprint).
3) SAML: add domain attestation via IdP assertion + integration tests (1 sprint).
4) Rollout: Feature-flagged canary in staging -> 5 pilot orgs on Dedicated -> expanded rollout (2 weeks per cohort).

Risks & Mitigations:
- False positives blocking legitimate invites: add soft-fail mode that creates a flagged invite and notifies admins instead of outright rejecting during canary.
- RBAC misconfiguration allowing privilege escalation: run a privilege matrix test suite and manual review by Security Eng before enabling for orgs.

Notes on related work and reasoning:
This ticket consolidates many prior invite-related patches and hardening work into a coherent platform-level control plane that plays nicely with RBAC v2 and SSO. It should reduce engineering debt from ad-hoc checks across frontend/backends and make audits and policy changes deterministic.

If we need to scope down: prioritize scoped team admins and basic allowlist/denylist first, defer SAML-based attestation to the next release window.
